metadata.title: Forget Files and Folders
metadata.purpose: Show viewers why the files-and-folders approach to Cowork is outdated and walk them through the new paradigm: Skills for recurring tasks, Projects for recurring context, AskUserQuestion for better prompting, and Wispr Flow for faster input.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: Forget Files and Folders?

beats.narration_text: Ciao. This is Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude: what is the right way to set up Claude Cowork today? Here's what that looks like — and the first answer is to stop doing what almost everyone taught you.

props.ask: What is the right way to set up Claude Cowork today?
props.answer_preview: Forget files and folders. Skills and Projects are the new setup…
props.command: Someone asked Claude: what is the right way to set up Claude Cowork today?

beats.narration_text: The old advice was files and folders — an about-me file, an outputs folder, a templates folder. It felt organized. But folders leak: even when you tell Cowork to ignore the outputs folder, it sometimes reads old outputs and poisons your current context. And files become impossible to maintain when you have a full-time job.

card.sub: Old outputs poisoned new sessions. Files never stayed current.

beats.narration_text: The new setup has two parts. Skills — a capability you call from anywhere with a slash command. It travels into any chat, and it even travels into other AI tools like Gemini and ChatGPT. Projects — a place you go to. Files and instructions stay loaded, Claude remembers across every chat inside that project, and you can share it with your team.

illustration.concept: Two-column comparison diagram. Left column: Skills — a slash command icon with the label '/linkedin-post', an arrow pointing outward showing it travels to Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT icons. Right column: Projects — a folder icon with a lock/memory badge, showing multiple chat bubbles staying inside one bounded space.
illustration.layout: Side-by-side columns on cream, thin dividing line, labels in EB Garamond at top of each column, icon details in warm ink

beats.narration_text: The decision rule: if it's something you can teach someone — a skill. If it's a specific context like a client or a campaign — a project. Use skills inside projects and that combination is how professionals run entire workflows without retyping anything.

card.sub: Teachable workflow = Skill. Specific context = Project.

beats.narration_text: The number one prompting trick is AskUserQuestion. Instead of writing a long, overthought prompt, you tell Claude: start by asking me questions. Claude then interviews you until it has enough context to do the job. The more context it draws out of you, the sharper the output. You can use it on the first prompt and keep using it every time you need more depth.

card.sub: Add: use the AskUserQuestion tool. Context follows. Quality follows.

beats.narration_text: You are the slow part of any Cowork session. Cowork can read a hundred thousand words in fifteen seconds. It waits for you to type at sixty words per minute. The fix is Wispr Flow — a dictation tool where you hold a key, talk, release, and your words appear in any app including Cowork's chatbox. Speaking gives more context than typing and keeps you in a natural flow state. The free tier is capped by the week — enough to know whether you like it.

card.sub: Wispr Flow: hold a key, talk, release. More context, less friction.

beats.narration_text: The one-hour setup from the infographic: six minutes to run your first task. Fifteen minutes to write files and connect integrations. Ten minutes to set global instructions. Ten minutes to build your folder structure. Ten minutes to create your first Cowork Project. Ten minutes for plugins and scheduling. Each block stands alone. You can stop after any one of them.

illustration.concept: A pie chart divided into six segments, each labeled with a time allocation and task name. Segments: 6 min Run first task (terracotta), 15 min Write + files, 10 min Set global instructions, 10 min Build folder, 10 min Create Cowork Project, 10 min Plugins + schedule. Hand-drawn on cream, single terracotta accent on the first segment.
illustration.layout: Centered pie chart with labels radiating outward, times in bold, task names in lighter weight

beats.narration_text: This week: create one Skill for something you keep explaining to Claude — a writing style, a task format, anything you've typed twice. Then create one Project for a client or a campaign and drop your most important context files in. Run one task using your Skill inside your Project. That is the complete new setup.

card.copy: One Skill, one Project, one task
card.sub: Build the setup that remembers so you don't have to.
